summary: Local Access Token (LAT): an opaque per-device string issued by the TP-Link IoT cloud in ThingInfo.localAccessToken (GET {iot-app-server}/v2/things, Authorization 'ut|<token>'). For TPAP pake 2 the app offers passcodes [md5_hex(cloud pw), SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT), SHA256_HEX_UPPER(cloud pw)]. The owner app moves the camera's admin credential to the LAT by sending changeAdminPassword (old 'empty', passwd SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT)) over the cloud passthrough, so after that only the LAT candidate works locally. Media :8800 digest uses SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT) in LAT mode.

items.description: The local access token (LAT) is issued by the TP-Link IoT cloud and delivered as field 'localAccessToken' of each ThingInfo in the IoT thing list. Gson default naming, so the JSON key is literally 'localAccessToken'. Only the thing list (and the QR-code bind reply) carries it; ThingDetail does not.

items.description: A second LAT source: the QR-code bind reply (POST {url}/v1/things/QRCode/bindDevice) returns localAccessToken, used by remote/SIM/NVR onboarding.

{iotAppServer} is not a literal host. Retrofit base is 'https://nbu.iot-app-server.app-v2' (a service id used as a placeholder host). An interceptor swaps that host for the real URL found in the account's appServerMap, which comes from POST {accountAppServerUrl}/api/v2/common/getAppServiceUrl {serviceIds:[...]} -> result.serviceUrls{serviceId:url}. Cached with an expiry; HTTP 422 or a missing/expired entry triggers a refresh.

items.description: How the app holds the LAT. ALCameraDevice.setThingDevice() copies ThingInfo.localAccessToken into CameraLATInfo (cloudRequestSuccess=true). CameraLATInfo is persisted in the device cache with cameraPasswordMode (lat|tp_password) and lastSyncLATTime. The cloud only hands out a LAT to accounts/devices inside a staged rollout ('LAT gray'); an empty LAT after a successful cloud fetch means the rollout is off for this device.

items.description: SPAKE2+ credentials offered by the app for tpap.pake containing 2 (passcode_type 'userpw'), in this order. The LAT candidate is SHA256 of the raw LAT string, hex, UPPER case (Locale default upper). Username for pake_register is md5_hex('admin') (lower) unless tpap.user_hash_type == 1, then SHA256_HEX_UPPER('admin'). Cipher suite [1], encryption aes_128_ccm, auth methods ['noc','spake2'].

For encrypt_type 3 (non-TPAP secure login) the app first logs in, reads nonce/device_confirm, and tests whether the camera still uses the TP-Link password (device_confirm starts with SHA256_UPPER(cnonce + SHA256_UPPER(pw) + nonce)). If not, it assumes LAT mode. In LAT mode the digest password is the raw LAT (hashed the same way as a password).

items.description: How the camera's admin credential becomes the LAT. Only the OWNER app does this, and only over a CLOUD transport (IoT-remote passthrough first, else legacy remote passthrough), never over LAN. The request is changeAdminPassword with old password literally 'empty' (hashed). After success the app stores cameraPasswordMode=LAT and lastSyncLATTime=now. A periodic job (needSyncDevicePasswordV3) re-pushes the cached LAT when the last sync is older than 24 h; when the rollout is off it pushes the TP-Link password instead.

items.description: At onboarding, cameras that support local_ctrl get a SPAKE2+ verifier instead of (or with) changeAdminPassword. The verifier is derived from md5_hex(cloud password), 16 random salt bytes, 5000 iterations. This is why candidate 1 (md5 of cloud password) works on freshly bound cameras that never received a LAT.

items.description: Local media (:8800 POST /stream) digest auth also follows the LAT. When the WWW-Authenticate challenge marks encrypt V3 and the device is in LAT mode, the digest password is SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT); otherwise SHA256_HEX_UPPER(cloud password) (non-V3: MD5_UPPER).

TDP 'owner' (32 hex) = md5_hex(localUserName) of the binding TP-Link account (email for email accounts). The app disables the LOCAL transport when it does not match the signed-in account, so only the owner logs in locally with these credentials.

evidence.snippet: getLocalUserName(): email for EMAIL register type

items.description: For non-camera IoT things (bulb quick setup) the app itself registers a LAT with the cloud: POST {thingUrl}/v2/things/{thingName}/sync-lat {localAccessToken: sha1_hex(cloud password)}. Not called for cameras; shown to explain the cloud field, not to derive the camera LAT.
What a desktop client should do for an encrypt_type ['4'] camera that rejects md5/sha256(cloud password) with -40401.

steps: 3. GET {iotAppServer}/v2/things?page=0&pageSize=100&deviceTypes=SMART.IPCAMERA&includeKasaShareDevices=true&includeExternalVendorDeviceInfo=true with Authorization 'ut|<token>' + app headers; page until total.
4. Pick the ThingInfo for the camera (thingName == cloud deviceId; check md5(thingName) against TDP device_id md5 if needed). Read localAccessToken.

5. TPAP pake_register/pake_share with passcode SHA256_HEX_UPPER(localAccessToken) (user md5_hex('admin')). Try it FIRST when a LAT exists: every wrong share counts toward the camera lock (-40404/-40408 sec_left).

6. If LAT is empty and both password candidates fail, the camera holds a LAT or password from an earlier sync. Only the owner can reset it, by pushing changeAdminPassword through the cloud passthrough (lat.sync.*). That overwrites the camera credential and needs explicit user consent.
value.cache: Store the LAT with fetch time; re-fetch when login fails or after 24 h.

unresolved.detail: The camera LAT is generated server-side; the APK never derives it locally for cameras (the bulb sync-lat path uses sha1_hex(cloud password), but there is no evidence that cameras use the same value). The client must fetch it from /v2/things.
Assumed thingName == cloud deviceId for cameras (ThingInfo has no deviceId field). Not traced; check against a live /v2/things reply.
The order of the j2 candidate list is verified. Whether com.tplink.tls tries every candidate after a -40401, or stops at the first failure, was not traced.
changeAdminPassword.ciphertext uses the RSA public key held in util.l (f158146d). The key literal was not extracted because the client only needs it for the optional sync path.
No REA commands were run. REA android commands do not work in this environment (orchestrator note), so all evidence is from JADX source.
